status: Visual proposals; attachment, independence and compatibility not validated

outputs.initial_prompt:
Edit and redesign the supplied image's Neo Modular Desk Clock itself, using it as the EDIT TARGET and visual identity reference. The user dislikes its bulky generic shape, wasted width at the left/right and the unused upper left/right corners. Create a clearly improved, elegant, practical, compact design rather than reproducing the original screenshot layout. Preserve the recognisable desk-clock-plus-powered-dock idea, serviceability, detachable modules, charcoal display and brushed metal. This is a photorealistic industrial design concept, not an instruction to engineer exact parts.
Use case: product-mockup. High-quality landscape 3:2 design board with ONE dominant large three-quarter hero taking most of the image. The screen is wide, low-profile, almost edge-to-edge, visually balanced, and sits securely on a compact satin-silver charging dock. Maintain generous legible clock digits. Carefully USE the two top corners of the clock: top-left contains a miniature detachable CAMERA cartridge, top-right contains a matching miniature detachable AI/Wi-Fi cartridge. Both are integrated flush into the upper corner geometry, like small precise removable modules with aligned edges, no bulky boxes sticking on top. The camera has one small lens, a subtle physical privacy shutter and a tiny status LED. The AI cartridge has a micro button and a tiny indication slit. Their silhouette is exceptionally minimal and family-consistent.
USE BOTH LEFT AND RIGHT SIDES intentionally: the slim left side contains a flush detachable AUDIO module and the slim right side contains a flush detachable ENVIRONMENT SENSOR module. The modules are genuine removable cassettes with a small believable seam and keyed mechanical guide, rather than decorative speakers moulded into the body. The side bays are visually integrated and not oversized. On the screen show 09:41, a very small tasteful live camera preview tile of a generic adult face, and discreet tiny sensor information. Do not use giant icons or decorative blobs.
The base retains a useful integrated wireless phone charging zone, a visually distinct USB-C input and USB-C output, and a built-in battery/power bank concept; these are space-planned, with no need to show several devices charging simultaneously. Consider the charging area as a useful integrated surface, not enormous empty wings. Include one generic phone on that area with subtle indication of charging. The clock's supporting structure bears the display mechanically; electrical pins do not support its weight. No exposed pogo contacts on the front surface.
Make the overall design premium, modern and minimal, with soft chamfers and a deliberate design language. Use charcoal / graphite and satin aluminum, black display, refined small accents, clear product geometry. Viewer should clearly see the camera and AI modules occupying upper corners AND the audio and sensor modules in the left/right edges.
At the bottom include two small but clear detail insets: (1) an angled exploded detail showing one corner cassette lifting out, with arrows, SAME exact cassette shape as in the hero, connector hidden/no pin count; (2) the entire dock unplugged from wall powering a generic phone by USB-C as a power-bank scenario. NO images of dissimilar different-sized modules masquerading as the same part.
Use very little typography, only exact English labels: "NEO MODULAR DESK CLOCK", "CAMERA", "AI + WI-FI", "AUDIO", "SENSOR", "POWER DOCK", "REMOVABLE MODULE", "POWER BANK MODE", and footer "CONCEPT DESIGN • Compatibility and performance require validation". No other text, no speculative power, number of contacts, price, certification marks or brand imitation. Frame everything fully within the image.
outputs.correction_prompt: Edit only the bottom-right small "POWER BANK MODE" inset of the supplied Neo Modular Desk Clock concept image. Keep the main hero, all product design, four module callouts, phone on the wireless pad, the bottom-left removable-module inset, all labels, footer, proportions and typography unchanged. In the bottom-right inset make the USB-C power-bank demonstration physically clear: the dock is unplugged from any wall adapter and a SINGLE SHORT cable visibly runs from the dock USB-C OUTPUT into the USB-C socket on the phone. Both cable ends are visibly inserted, with the complete cable uninterrupted in view. Place the phone next to the dock to make the plug connection obvious. No wireless charging symbol is needed in this inset. The clock and its modules stay attached and unchanged. Do not add ratings or claims.

outputs.initial_prompt:
Create a SECOND new illustrated concept board using the attached image as the edit target and styling reference for the Neo modular clock's family. Show where the clock's removable modules can be attached on OTHER products. Maintain an exact single consistent physical module design across all panels: compact understated satin charcoal rounded-rectangular cartridge with a tiny side USB-C port and keyed slide/clip receiver; camera variant has one lens, physical privacy shutter, small status light; AI variant has a minimal button, grille and small status light; sensor variant has a tiny display. Each type is the SAME SHAPE and SAME RELATIVE SIZE when shown detached, installed or carried. Do not enlarge or redesign the same module for another host.
Design a high-quality landscape 3:2 board titled exactly "ONE MODULE, MANY PRODUCTS" with four separate clear visual scenarios and spacious clean layout:
1. "LAPTOP + CAMERA": slim camera cartridge attaches at the top of a generic laptop display via an explicitly visible compact clip / USB-C adapter cable, using the SAME camera cartridge as the clock. Screen shows a friendly video-call preview with a generic adult face; privacy shutter/indicator visible.
2. "ROBOT + AI": compact four-wheeled desktop robot uses the SAME AI cartridge slotted into a purpose-designed host receiver; show it as a product concept, no fictional mature ecosystem.
3. "WEARABLE + AI": the same AI cartridge is detached and put into a simple wearable clip with its own button, microphone/speaker grille, and power provided by the cartridge or the clip; show a hand holding it with no ambiguous dangling power wire. Small Wi-Fi mark communicates connectivity; do not promise offline AI.
4. "ROOM MONITOR + SENSOR": matching sensor module attaches by a visible adapter to a small desk environmental monitor; screen shows simple illustrative temperature and humidity readings, not air-quality certification.
At the bottom show the original clock with two minimal flush corner module bays, SAME camera and AI cartridges, and a concise key: "Same module • compatible host or adapter". Add a tiny line of separate standalone representations: the camera with record button and the AI cartridge with a microphone and button, each powered independently by its own battery or external USB-C, illustrating real standalone function.
Keep the composition clean and minimal; do not include elaborate technical diagrams, pin counts, numerical dimensions, wattages, certifications or claims of existing compatibility. Every host adapter is conceptual and shown. No brand imitation. Footer exact: "PRODUCT CONCEPTS • Compatibility and independent use require validation".

Add appropriate tiny grille, battery or USB-C in detached AI mode without changing overall silhouette. Replace ONLY the lower-left "ORIGINAL CLOCK" rendering with an accurate miniature of the SECOND reference's REFINED wide edge-to-edge clock: camera fitted flush in the top-left corner, the matching AI module fitted flush in the top-right corner, slim audio module left and sensor module right, silver powered base. Reuse the shapes, orientation and relative scale of the camera and AI modules on the actual clock from reference 2 in every corresponding scene, so the same cartridges can plausibly move between hosts; host clip adapters may differ.
